clue.text: Finding two pence in water brings a lump in one's throat

indicators.note: the two pennies are found sitting in the middle of the phrase for water

parts.note: Adam's ale is an old jocular name for plain drinking water
P is the abbreviation for a penny, so two of them give PP

explanation.surface: Someone discovers coins in their drink and gets choked up.
explanation.walkthrough: PP goes inside ADAMS ALE, splitting it as ADAMS A-PP-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the visible bulge of the larynx at the front of the neck.

clue.text: Top expert pinches millions

indicators.note: to pinch something is to grip it tightly, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A leading specialist is caught stealing large sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the acme is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Don't start — suspended for fishing!

indicators.note: telling the word not to start means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: something suspended is hanging loose, or dangling

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea not to begin a sport, which has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended' looks like a ban on fishing, but it means hanging; drop the first letter D of DANGLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: angling is the sport of fishing with rod and line.

clue.text: Bank facility for putting up with brothers, for example

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it, so putting up with is standing
a religious order, such as one of monks or friars, is made up of brothers

explanation.surface: A bank service that tolerates monks.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing order is an instruction to a bank to make a regular fixed payment.

clue.text: Stupidly tiptoe in to make a request

indicators.note: doing something stupidly suggests the letters are jumbled carelessly

explanation.surface: Creeping into a room clumsily to ask for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' rearranges the eight letters of TIPTOE and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition is to make a formal appeal or request to an authority.

clue.text: Primate depicted in Constable mural

indicators.note: the answer is shown within the painted letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An animal painted in a wall picture by the artist Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter; the answer spans constab-LE MUR-al.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a tree-dwelling primate found in Madagascar.

clue.text: Fruit regularly seen in doctor's bag

indicators.note: the picked letters are found sitting inside the doctor's abbreviation

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Some fruit glimpsed inside a physician's medical case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes R and I from Fruit, placed inside GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip, short for gripsack, is a travelling bag.

clue.text: Warning traitor regularly on diplomacy

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next
picking out letters at regular intervals, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people diplomatically

explanation.surface: A turncoat is cautioned about relations with other states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of traitor; 'on' in a down clue puts that run above the diplomacy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading someone the riot act is idiom for giving them a stern warning.

clue.text: Such examples end respect for revision

indicators.note: letters put up for revision are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A proposal to reconsider and stop showing deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For revision' rearranges the ten letters of END RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Precedents are earlier cases taken as examples to follow.

clue.text: Review degree given for hot rock

parts.note: a review is a periodical, and a magazine is shortened to mag
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A critique of an academic qualification in exchange for a hot stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface.

clue.text: Unruly mob sent to film location

indicators.note: an unruly crowd is disorderly, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd is dispatched to where a movie is being shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges the nine letters of MOB SENT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tombstone, Arizona, is the Wild West town where many films, including one of that name, are set.

clue.text: Avoiding directors, this may go to the wall

definitions.text: this may go to the wall

parts.note: to skirt something is to go round it, avoiding it
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Dodging the management, this firm may go bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to the wall' suggests business failure, but the board literally runs along the base of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirting board is fixed along the bottom of an interior wall.

clue.text: Dine out and finish uncertain

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: to terminate something is to finish it

explanation.surface: Eat at a restaurant and end up not sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is the anagram signal for Dine alone; 'finish' supplies the rest unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: indeterminate means not fixed or settled, so uncertain.

clue.text: Picture young bird with fine taste

parts.note: a chick is a newly hatched bird
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a lick is a small taste of something

explanation.surface: A drawing of a fledgling with discerning palate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick flick is a film aimed at women, and a picture is a film.

clue.text: Elated, when hands go up for film

parts.note: high means in great spirits
at midday both hands of a clock point straight up

explanation.surface: Feeling great as a crowd raises their hands to answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' suggest people raising arms, but they are clock hands.
explanation.definitionFit: High Noon is a 1952 Western starring Gary Cooper.

clue.text: Standing, with no right, for representation

indicators.note: having no particular letter means it is taken out

parts.note: stature is reputation or standing

explanation.surface: Someone's reputation suffers when they lack any entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast representation of a figure.

clue.text: Ancestor's warning on creature of the woods

definitions.note: read as ancestor is, so the 's links to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of a ball in flight
a bear is a large forest animal

explanation.surface: A forebear shouts a warning about a forest animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a forebear is a forefather or ancestor.

clue.text: Inexperienced, and depressed by coastal state

indicators.note: one piece stands beside the other

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state on the Pacific coast
low means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: Someone green and gloomy because of where they live by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means young and lacking experience of life.

clue.text: Doctor rues all old awards

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician regrets everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is a verb rearranging RUES ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel wreaths were awarded as honours to victors in ancient times.

clue.text: Miserable Irish county players

parts.note: Down is a county in Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: An unhappy troupe of actors from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: downcast means dejected or low in spirits.

clue.text: A rule on the radio is put on trial

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: A gives A; a reign is a period of rule by a monarch

explanation.surface: A regulation broadcast is challenged in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to call them before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Establishment figure?

parts.note: not a pillar of society, but a person who was part of setting up a club or society at the start

explanation.surface: A pillar of the ruling class.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who helped found an organisation is one of its original members.

clue.text: Paper encompassing student's sphere of knowledge

indicators.note: one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: An essay containing what a learner knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain, as in the realm of science.

clue.text: Nothing more than water

definitions.meaning: ... means only, as in a ... child

explanation.definitionFit: Mere is an adjective for no more than, and a noun for a small lake.

clue.text: Drunken English occupying poor Britain leave at last

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes up a place inside the rearranged country
a poor version is a mangled one, so the letters are jumbled
the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A tipsy Englishman in a depressed Britain finally goes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges BRITAIN as INBRIAT; E goes inside, then the last letter of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriate is an adjective meaning intoxicated.

clue.text: A tall story — over very quick

indicators.note: the lie is laid over the abbreviation, covering it

parts.note: a tall story is an untruth, a lie

explanation.surface: A far-fetched tale told at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in the old sense means living, as in the quick and the dead.

clue.text: Jack is simply showing a light touch

indicators.note: the answer is displayed within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A man named Jack demonstrates delicate handling.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across jac-K IS S-imply.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss can describe any gentle contact, as when a ball just kisses another.

clue.text: The cheek to cross leader of rebels shows lack of caution

indicators.note: one piece goes across the middle of the other

parts.note: impudence is cheek or insolence

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter

explanation.surface: Defying the head of an insurgency is reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is rashness, the failure to show care or caution.
